messages.author: 55cb20da3fe82e18
messages.subject: Product Roadmap
parts:
Great package/idea - this was exactly what I was researching and I'm glad there is an effort to build a full solution (and enterprise grade) 

Few questions about what the product road-map is and what features we should expect in the upcoming releases. I think the basic widgets are great start and serve a lot of the use cases - as long as their is a mapping for displaying data.frames/lists/matrices/etc

Couple of questions:

  • Is there a plan to add validation for user input fields client side i.e. a input field should be a number or string, etc 
  • How are server side errors propagated to the user/UI - for example, if you user requests invalid date range or the data doesn't exist, how would you display that information gracefully to the UI
  • Are there plans to add authentication support i.e. users, groups, permissions per view, etc (something similar to the django admin module which comes for free out of the box)
  • Would there be support for automatically updating the UI without any user input e.g. push updates to the data to the user.
  • Are there any limitations in using existing R packages like ggplot2/googleVis/ or tikz images 
  • How would you stitch together more complicated applications - for example, if you expand on your stocks example and add another view which shows fundamental time-series data, how would the navigation work. 
  • How would you add static data to pages 
  • What other widgets are you guys planning on adding
Thanks

-Haider

messages.author: f806781d102fe0ab
messages.subject: Re: Product Roadmap
parts: • Is there a plan to add validation for user input fields client side i.e. a input field should be a number or string, etc
Sure, that seems like a really good candidate for our next release.
• How are server side errors propagated to the user/UI - for example, if you user requests invalid date range or the data doesn't exist, how would you display that information gracefully to the UI

The easiest way right now is to simply use R's default error handling, e.g. stop("Invalid date range"). When these errors make it all the way to an output without being caught, they are displayed in place of the output. The default style is for the error to appear in red, prepended with the word "Error:" in bold, but that is all customizable using CSS.
• Are there plans to add authentication support i.e. users, groups, permissions per view, etc (something similar to the django admin module which comes for free out of the box)

Definitely user authentication. I don't know what granularity at which the permissions will apply. If you could describe the scenario you have in mind for django-like permissions, it would be hugely helpful. (You're welcome to e-mail me off-list if you don't want to publicize details of your app.)
• Would there be support for automatically updating the UI without any user input e.g. push updates to the data to the user.

Yes, we have not written up examples of this yet but the pieces are there.

The most common way that changes ripple through the system is through users touching inputs, but another way that we already support is time-based invalidation. Here's an example I just wrote that has two different components that are varying over time:

Demo: http://glimmer.rstudio.com/jcheng/time/
Source: https://gist.github.com/4044364

This might not be intuitive yet if you're still getting your head around reactive programming, but the point is that the "invalidateLater" function is all that is needed to build, say, a reactiveFileInput function that pushes changed values through the system. An intrepid Shiny user could build such a function now, but if you wait until the next release we can probably save you the trouble.
• Are there any limitations in using existing R packages like ggplot2/googleVis/ or tikz images

No problem with ggplot2, and in general visualizations that write to R's default graphics device should work fine. googleVis will need some customization to work with Shiny, similar to the kind of stuff Markus had to do to get googleVis to work with R Markdown. I'm not familiar with tikz.

• How would you stitch together more complicated applications - for example, if you expand on your stocks example and add another view which shows fundamental time-series data, how would the navigation work.

Currently Shiny is focused on single-page apps, so you'd need to integrate all the views into a single page. Tabs actually work pretty nicely for that in a lot of cases: http://glimmer.rstudio.com/mosaic/CIgeometry/
• How would you add static data to pages
Can you be more specific about "static data"?
• What other widgets are you guys planning on adding

We don't have anything specific planned right now, we're just waiting to see what people request.

I'll add that we are more excited about helping folks in the community to design and package their own widgets that can be easily used by all Shiny users.

Thanks for the great questions--hope that helps!

messages.author: 55cb20da3fe82e18
messages.subject: Re: Product Roadmap
parts:
By static data, I meant including standard header and footer html content like logos, etc. It's not a big deal but curious if there is a way to support that.

Also, would it be possible to add "export" like functionality, specifically for output plots I.e. display a plot but also provide a link to download the plot as a pdf for higher resolution


Regarding the django-admin functionality - I didn't have any specific requirements besides authentication. The other nice thing about the admin model is that it allows for per model/data permissions so that normal users can see pages/data relevant to them and a admin user could see all data. Again to begin with probably not a big deal, but I think for this to be week rounded for a commercial use, these things would be great.

Also please let me know if the direction that I'm going in is within your strategic scope of this product or if you see it as a building block for others to use.

Thanks

messages.author: f806781d102fe0ab
messages.subject: Re: Product Roadmap
parts:
Yes, there are a number of options. The first thing to know is that all of the calls we use in ui.R/shinyUI are just HTML generating functions. For example, if you type this at the R console:

> textInput('foo', 'Foo')
[1] "<label>Foo</label>\n<input id=\"foo\" type=\"text\" value=\"\"/>"
attr(,"html")
[1] TRUE

You can see that the textInput function doesn't do anything magical, it just outputs HTML. You can output HTML yourself in a number of ways.

1) You can write your HTML as a string and wrap it in a call to the HTML function.
2) You can use the tag generating functions that Shiny comes with.
3) You can put your HTML in a separate file, and include it.

I've included examples of all 3 in this gist: https://gist.github.com/4052973
You can run it with runGist('https://gist.github.com/4052973').

If you have other assets--CSS, images, JavaScript files--that you want to include in your application, you can create a www directory inside of your Shiny app directory. Any files you put in there will be available to your page. You should refer to them with relative URLs. For example, if you had www/logo.png, you would do HTML('<img src="logo.png"/>') or img(src="logo.png").

If anything about that is unclear please let me know.

As for the auth stuff, that sounds very much like what we have in mind. So far I don't think anything you've mentioned sounds out of scope for us. Thanks for the valuable feedback!

messages.author: f806781d102fe0ab
messages.subject: Re: Product Roadmap
parts:
There's currently no component that combines an output table with reactive inputs. You could either cobble together one using reactiveUI and the HTML builder commands, or someone could write such a component and release it as part of a package.

I suspect (and hope) that as people become more fluent with Shiny you will start to see 3rd party Shiny components appearing on GitHub and eventually CRAN, I'm sure there are a lot of controls that would be interesting to a lot of people, especially fancier tables.
